written.description: Chains recon, exploitation and post-exploitation, then carries a finding further than a report: it writes the fix and opens a pull request on your repository.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(recon): wildcard entries in the Domain-batch target list

A Domain batch could only ever scan hostnames you already knew: subdomain
discovery was force-disabled for the whole run, because a bare root yields
prefixes ['.'] and parse_target treats a '.'-only list as NOT filtered mode,
which would have silently enumerated a domain meant to be probed at the apex.

`*.example.com` (or `*example.com`) now makes that ONE group run the same full
discovery a Single Domain project runs, while every other line in the list is
still scanned exactly as written. The decision is per group, carried as a '*'
sentinel beside the existing '.', and the run-wide force-off narrows to "no
group asked to enumerate". Listing the bare domain next to the wildcard also
scans the apex - that is what the preview's new Root checkbox writes, since
root inclusion has never been a field.

A wildcard must name a registrable domain: the batch grouping rule is
last-two-labels, so `*.co.uk` would enumerate a public suffix. It is refused
using the curated list origin_discovery already owns for the same reason.

Scope became editable after creation in the project form only. It stays
create_only over MCP because that one flag also governs whether a parsed Rules
of Engagement document may write a field, and an untrusted document must never
re-point the platform's targets.

Fixes found while reviewing and running this end to end:

- A host listed beside a wildcard was re-resolved only when discovery returned
  nothing at all, so when enumeration succeeded but missed it, that host
  reached the scan file with no DNS and no IP: present, and invisible to every
  later phase.
- A crt.sh non-200 produced no log line whatsoever. requests does not raise on
  5xx and the branch had no else, so a 502 - which crt.sh returns regularly -
  read exactly like "this domain has no certificates".
- A discovered hostname could drag the scanner inward. Enumeration adopts the
  target owner's DNS, and `localhost.<domain> -> 127.0.0.1` is a real, common
  record; nothing downstream re-checked, so it was scanned. Discovered names
  resolving to loopback, link-local, unspecified or multicast are now dropped
  and logged. Private ranges are deliberately kept, because internal estates
  are a supported target, as are the apex and anything the operator typed.

Also carries an unrelated in-flight change to the MCP scope checklist
(ScopeChecklist, scopeCopy, ReconLogsDrawer) committed together at the
maintainer's request.

Verified end to end against vendor-published test targets: one enumerating
group and two literal groups in a single run, with `subdomain_discovery` in
modules_executed for the wildcard group only, the apex resolved and present,
and Domain.wildcard_mode set on the enumerated domain alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
